memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Each one who crosses over to those already counted is to give a half shekel, according to the sanctuary shekel, which weighs twenty gerahs. This half shekel is an offering to the Lord. All who cross over, those twenty years old or more, are to give an offering to the Lord. The rich are not to give more than a half shekel and the poor are not to give less when you make the offering to the Lord to atone for your lives." - Exodus 30:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Look carefully at what God commands here. Everyone pays the same — half a shekel, no more and no less. The rich may not give extra, and the poor may not give less. In a world where wealth usually buys advantage, God levels the ground completely.

The reason is that this payment was atonement money, covering their lives. And no one's life is worth more than another's before God. A wealthy man could not purchase greater standing, and a poor man was not valued less. At the place of atonement, everyone stood on identical footing.

This is the gospel's levelling too. Paul writes that there is no difference, for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, and all are justified freely by His grace through the redemption that came by Christ Jesus (Rom 3:22-24). The successful and the struggling come the same way — by grace, through the same Saviour, at the same price which none of us paid ourselves. Nobody upgrades their salvation, and nobody receives a lesser version of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I ever assume some people are more valuable to God than others?
Am I secure that my standing before God rests entirely on Christ, not my status?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, at the cross the ground is completely level. Thank You that my standing rests on Christ alone, not my status. Help me see every person as equally precious to You. Amen.
